title: Projectile Target Challenge: Pick Angle and Speed
description: A launcher sits at the left end of a flat 70 m field with marks every 10 m. A blue target disc with a yellow flag sits down the field. Set the launch angle and speed, then press Launch: the orange ball flies its arc over about two seconds, leaving a trail. The previous arc stays as a faded grey line. Readouts give landing distance, miss distance and side, flight time, highest point, launches used and targets hit. Hit 3 targets (30 m, 45 m, 18 m) within 10 launches.

game.objective: Hit 3 targets (at 30 m, 45 m, then 18 m) by landing within 1.5 m of each centre, using no more than 10 launches.
game.hint: At the same speed, angles that add up to 90° (like 30° and 60°) land at the same distance, and 45° goes farthest. Doubling the speed makes the shot go four times as far.

assumptions: Simplified simulation: no air resistance, ball starts at ground level on flat ground, drawn larger than a real ball so it is easy to see.
Gravity is 9.8 m/s² straight down; horizontal speed stays constant and only vertical speed changes. Landing distance = speed² × sin(2 × angle) ÷ 9.8 exactly in this model.
A hit is a landing within 1.5 m of the target centre, both edges counted (the blue disc has radius 1.5 m). Targets come in a fixed order: 30 m, 45 m, 18 m.
Every flight is shown over about two seconds, so screen time does not match the flight-time readout. The ball is a point for the physics; the flight ends when it returns to ground height.
Real balls are slowed by air and land shorter, especially at high speed; the 45° best angle is exact only without air. Longest shot is about 64 m (25 m/s at 45°).
